# Forward-Mode vs Reverse-Mode Automatic Differentiation

Automatic differentiation computes exact derivatives of programs using the chain rule applied to elementary operations — not approximations (finite differences) or expression swell (symbolic diff).

## Why Not Symbolic or Numerical Differentiation?

Symbolic: expression swell, no control flow. Numerical (finite diff): O(h) error, O(n) passes for n inputs, float rounding issues. Both are impractical for neural network training.

## Dual Numbers and Forward-Mode AD

Dual number (a, ḃ) with ε²=0. Evaluation with (x, v) gives f(x) as primal and ∇f(x)·v as tangent — a Jacobian-vector product (JVP) in one pass. Full gradient costs n passes.

## Reverse-Mode AD: Vector-Jacobian Products

Adjoint ā = ∂L/∂a. Propagated backward: for y = f(x), x̄ += ȳ·(∂f/∂x). One backward pass gives full ∇L ∈ ℝⁿ regardless of n. Standard for neural networks (n_params >> 1, n_outputs = 1).

| Mode | Computes | Cost | Efficient when |
|------|----------|------|----------------|
| Forward (JVP) | ∇f(x)·v | 1× forward | few inputs |
| Reverse (VJP) | uᵀ·J | 1× forward + backward | few outputs (neural nets) |

## The Wengert List (Tape)

Forward pass records all operations and inputs. Backward pass replays tape in reverse, computing VJPs and accumulating adjoints. PyTorch: dynamic graph built at runtime. JAX: traces to Jaxpr, compiled via XLA.

```python
# JAX composable transforms
grad_fn = jax.grad(loss_fn)                   # reverse-mode gradient
primals, tangents = jax.jvp(fn, (x,), (v,))  # forward-mode JVP
jac = jax.jacobian(fn)                        # full Jacobian via VJPs
```

## Gradient Checkpointing

Cache only √L activations instead of all L. Recompute intermediates during backward. Memory: O(√L) vs O(L). Compute: +33%. Flash Attention uses tiled recomputation for O(N) memory vs O(N²).

## Higher-Order Derivatives

jax.grad(jax.grad(f)) computes second derivative. Forward-over-reverse gives HVPs: jax.jvp(jax.grad(f)). Enables MAML, neural ODEs, physics-informed networks.
